sentences.en: But there's a need to understand the geology of Britain.
sentences.zh: 但当时有一种理解英国地质的需求。

sentences.en: And so therefore, when you're looking at the geology, inevitably, you're starting to find all these fossils.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你研究地质时，不可避免地会开始发现所有这些化石。

sentences.en: And there's just a kind of curiosity about it, and a kind of range of kind of mingled amateurs and men of science who kind of just put it together.
sentences.zh: 人们对它有着一种好奇心，并且有一群由业余爱好者和科学人士交织成的群体把这些碎片拼凑在了一起。

sentences.en: So I think that one of the things that's really interesting about dinosaurs is the way that their discovery is kind of associated with the Industrial Revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得关于恐龙最有趣的事情之一，就是它们的发现与工业革命息息相关。

sentences.en: So even though they are expressions of a kind of unimaginably distant past, and people find it incredibly destabilizing, of course, to realize that actually time is much,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管它们是某种难以想象的遥远过去的表现形式，人们自然会觉得极度颠覆，因为他们意识到时间实际上比

sentences.en: much deeper than they'd anticipated,
sentences.zh: 他们预期的要漫长、漫长得多，

sentences.en: they are also kind of cutting edge, which is why they appear at the Crystal Palace, which is this great monument to British know-how and get up and go.
sentences.zh: 但它们也同样处于时代的前沿，这就是为什么它们会出现在水晶宫——这座彰显英国专业技术与进取精神的伟大纪念碑中。

sentences.en: And it's why in Bleak House, in the opening paragraph, Dickens fixes on, you know, he describes the mists that are kind of filling London.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么在《荒凉山庄》的开篇段落中，狄更斯会聚焦于——他描述了弥漫伦敦的雾气。

sentences.en: And he says that it wouldn't be a surprise to see a Megalosaurus walking up Hoban Hill.
sentences.zh: 他说，看到一只斑龙走上霍本山也不会让人感到意外。

sentences.en: He is, you know, that's a cutting edge reference.
sentences.zh: 他用了，你知道的，那是一个非常超前的引用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Absolutely cutting edge reference.
sentences.zh: 绝对是极其前沿的引用。

sentences.en: So it's sort of pushing the frontiers of science, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像在开拓科学的前沿，对吧？

sentences.en: I suppose forwards and backwards, as it were.
sentences.zh: 我猜既向前推进，也向后追溯，可以这么说。

sentences.en: Now, I was about to say, we've got a few questions about the Victorians.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，我们还有几个关于维多利亚时代的问题。

sentences.en: So maybe this is a good place to do them.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许是个开始讲它们的好地方。

sentences.en: Alyssa McCarthy has a question about gentleman collectors.
sentences.zh: 阿丽莎·麦卡锡有一个关于绅士收藏家的问题。

sentences.en: How much are gentleman collectors driving this sort of, the progress in paleontology?
sentences.zh: 绅士收藏家在多大程度上推动了古生物学这类学科的进展？

sentences.en: And Mark Kirk Alves has a question that I wanted to ask, which is about Mary Anning.
sentences.zh: 马克·柯克·阿尔维斯也有一个我想问的问题，关于玛丽·安宁。

sentences.en: So Mary Anning operated Lyon Regis, and basically, I think by internationally approved binding laws, all British children now have to learn about Mary Anning.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安宁活跃在莱姆里吉斯，基本上，我认为按照国际公认的成文法规，现在所有英国儿童都必须了解玛丽·安宁。

sentences.en: And it's unthinkable that they don't.
sentences.zh: 而且不了解是不可想象的。

sentences.en: Now, Mark Kirk Alves says, did she really play a role or were we just desperate to make the subject relatable to girls?
sentences.zh: 现在，马克·柯克·阿尔维斯说，她真的发挥了作用，还是我们只是极力想让这个学科对女孩更有吸引力？

sentences.en: So is it gentleman collectors?
sentences.zh: 所以，是绅士收藏家吗？

sentences.en: Does Mary Anning matter?
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安宁重要吗？

sentences.en: What's the story?
sentences.zh: 这背后的故事是什么？

sentences.en: It is gentleman collectors, because William Buckland and Gideon Mantell and people like that, you know, they're all gentlemen, essentially.
sentences.zh: 确实是绅士收藏家，因为威廉·巴克兰、基甸·曼特尔以及诸如此类的人，你知道的，本质上他们全都是绅士。

sentences.en: And you have to be a gentleman.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须是一位绅士。

sentences.en: You have to be of a gentle breeding and you have to be a man to get your papers accepted by the requisite societies, which is why Mary Anning is marginalised through her life.
sentences.zh: 你的出身必须高贵，而且必须是个男性，论文才能被相关的学术社团接受，这就是为什么玛丽·安宁一生都被边缘化。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, she is an astonishing figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她是一位令人惊叹的人物。

sentences.en: So just give us a sense of who she is, Tom, for those listeners who don't know.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，能给我们大致讲讲她是谁吗，为了那些不了解的听众。

sentences.en: So the reason that I haven't mentioned Mary Anning up to now is that this is about dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 我到现在还没提到玛丽·安宁的原因是，这期节目讲的是恐龙。

sentences.en: And dinosaurs are land-
sentences.zh: 而恐龙是陆地的——

sentences.en: She's fossils, right?
sentences.zh: 她研究的是化石，对吧？

sentences.en: She's absolutely fossils.
sentences.zh: 她绝对是研究化石的。

sentences.en: Dinosaurs are land-based.
sentences.zh: 恐龙是陆栖的。

sentences.en: Mary Anning is discovering creatures that swam in the seas.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安宁发现的是在海里游动的生物。

sentences.en: So at the time, most of Dorset was underwater.
sentences.zh: 所以在当时，多塞特郡大部分都在水面以下。

sentences.en: So that's why Mary Anning is finding ichthyosaurs, which kind of look like, you know, dolphins.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么玛丽·安宁能找到鱼龙，它们看起来有点像，你知道的，海豚。

sentences.en: She's finding plesiosaurs, which is the Loch Ness monster type, the long neck and the flippers.
sentences.zh: 她发现了蛇颈龙，也就是尼斯湖水怪那种类型的，长脖子和鳍。

sentences.en: She is discovering pterosaurs.
sentences.zh: 她正在发现翼龙。

sentences.en: She's identifying coprolites, which are basically fossilised turds.
sentences.zh: 她识别了粪石，也就是基本上是化石化的粪便。

sentences.en: And she's an amazing, amazing pioneer.
sentences.zh: 而且她是一位了不起、了不起的先驱。

sentences.en: And she comes from the most kind of grinding poverty.
sentences.zh: 她出身于极度困窘的贫困之中。

sentences.en: She, as a child, was she was under a tree with three women and lightning struck.
sentences.zh: 她小时候，曾和三个女人在一棵树下，结果遭到了雷击。

sentences.en: And all the women died of the lightning strike and she survived.
sentences.zh: 所有那些女人都在雷击中丧生了，而她活了下来。

sentences.en: And the theory was, in line, Regis, this has kind of given her a spark, her curiosity.
sentences.zh: 当时莱姆里吉斯的理论认为，这某种程度上激发了她的火花和好奇心。

sentences.en: I mean, she could, you know, she learned to read and write, but she had no real kind of scholarly background greater than that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她，你知道的，她学会了读写，但除此之外她并没有什么真正的学术背景。

sentences.en: And yet she achieves this kind of revolution in the understanding of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 然而她却对过去世界的理解实现了这种变革。

sentences.en: The scale of her discoveries and her ability to understand what it is that she's finding is amazing.
sentences.zh: 她发现的规模以及她理解自己所发现事物的能力令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And they get essentially they kind of get the gentleman's scholars are like jackals feeding on her kills and she doesn't really get any of it.
sentences.zh: 而绅士学者们基本上就像在她的战利品上进食的胡狼一样，她自己却几乎一无所得。

sentences.en: But there's one hero in this, which is a guy called Henry de la Biche, who is an illustrator,
sentences.zh: 但这里面有一个英雄，那就是一个名叫亨利·德拉比奇的家伙，他是一位插画师，

sentences.en: who illustrates what is effectively the very first illustration of a prehistoric landscape.
sentences.zh: 他绘制了可以说是历史上第一幅史前风景画。

sentences.en: And it's in Latin, it's called Dorset as it was a long, long ago.
sentences.zh: 它用拉丁语命名，意思是“很久很久以前的多塞特”。

sentences.en: And it shows long-necked plesiosaurs kind of crunching on pterosaurs and it shows ichthyosaurs.
sentences.zh: 画面展示了长脖子的蛇颈龙在啃食翼龙，还展示了鱼龙。

sentences.en: And there's, you know, Marianne has basically discovered that she's at France's thesis that faeces can be fossilised.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，玛丽安娜基本上发现了——也就是她证明了粪便可以被石化。

sentences.en: And there's, I think it's a plesiosaur who's in the process of being munched to death, literally shitting himself.
sentences.zh: 我想其中有一只蛇颈龙正在被活活啃食，字面意思上它正吓得屁滚尿流。

sentences.en: And you can see this, these kind of turns dropping down to the bottom of the sediment, you know, the bottom of the sea,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这些粪便掉落到沉积物底部，你知道的，海底，

sentences.en: where they in due course will be fossilised and then be discovered by Marianne.
sentences.zh: 它们在那里适时地变成化石，然后被玛丽安娜发现。

sentences.en: So she's a massive figure, but she's not discovering dinosaurs because Lyme Regis is, you know, in the Mesozoic sea, not land.
sentences.zh: 所以她是一个庞大的人物，但她发现的不是恐龙，因为莱姆里吉斯处于中生代的海域，而不是陆地。

sentences.en: So I wanted to ask about Christianity because we're in the mid-Victorian period, the age of Darwin, but I think we should take a break.
sentences.zh: 所以我想问关于基督教的问题，因为我们身处维多利亚时代中期，达尔文的时代，但我想我们应该休息一下。

sentences.en: So people have got that to look forward to, which is very exciting.
sentences.zh: 所以大家可以期待接下来的内容，这非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: We'll talk about that, then we'll get into America, and then we'll talk about 20th century dinosaurs and dinosaurs, kind of metaphorical meanings and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们谈完这个，然后进入美国部分，接着聊聊20世纪的恐龙以及恐龙的隐喻意义等等。

sentences.en: And we'll do all that after the break, so don't go away.
sentences.zh: 我们在休息之后再讨论所有这些，所以请不要离开。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的剩余部分》。

sentences.en: We are talking dinosaurs and the way, the history of the ways in which they've been understood.
sentences.zh: 我们正在讨论恐龙以及人类理解它们的方式的历史。

sentences.en: So Tom Holland, we have reached the sort of mid-19th century.
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆·霍兰，我们已经进入了19世纪中叶左右。

sentences.en: There have been tremendous breakthroughs in the understanding of dinosaurs, the coining of the word dinosaur, for example,
sentences.zh: 人类在理解恐龙方面取得了巨大的突破，例如“恐龙”这个词的诞生，

sentences.en: the exhibition of kind of recreations of dinosaurs and so on.
sentences.zh: 恐龙复原模型的展览等等。

sentences.en: So the big question is, how does this affect what is a very, you know, God-fearing age?
sentences.zh: 所以最大的问题是，这对一个非常敬畏上帝的时代产生了怎样的影响？

sentences.en: What's the, this is the age of Darwinism, obviously, but it's also an age of tremendous sort of interest in Christianity, tremendous debate and so on.
sentences.zh: 这是达尔文主义的时代，显而易见，但这也是一个对基督教充满极高兴趣、激烈辩论等等的时代。

sentences.en: Do dinosaurs break people's faith or do people fit them into the Christian story?
sentences.zh: 恐龙打破了人们的信仰，还是人们把它们融入了基督教的故事中？

sentences.en: What do they do?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做的？

sentences.en: I don't think dinosaurs per se particularly affect people.
sentences.zh: 我不认为恐龙本身对人们有什么特别的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, Buckland, you know, as I said, he becomes the dean of Westminster.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我所说，巴克兰后来成为了威斯敏斯特大教堂的院长。

sentences.en: It's how dinosaurs fit into Darwinism really starts to shake people's faith because, of course, the idea that dinosaurs are, you know,
sentences.zh: 真正开始动摇人们信仰的是恐龙如何融入达尔文主义，因为当然，恐龙的概念是，

sentences.en: which is still there in the way that we use dinosaur as a kind of pejorative to this day.
sentences.zh: 这种看法直到今天仍然存在于我们把“恐龙”当作贬义词的使用中。

sentences.en: This idea that there were these ancient monsters and then they kind of became superseded because they were kind of run out of town by evolutionary forces,
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，曾有这些古老的怪物，然后它们被淘汰了，因为它们被进化力量赶出了历史舞台，

sentences.en: which kind of beds in pretty quickly because the uptick in the discovery of dinosaurs, particularly in America, coincides with the explosion of kind of Darwinism.
sentences.zh: 这种观念确立得相当快，因为恐龙发现量的激增，特别是在美国，与达尔文主义的爆发同时发生。

sentences.en: And it's that really that unsettles people.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点真正让人们感到不安。

sentences.en: So I'll give you an example of a man whose faith does get very radically affected by it, but it's the interplay between his discovery of dinosaurs and the Darwinism.
sentences.zh: 所以我举一个人的例子，他的信仰确实受到了极其深刻的影响，但这是他发现恐龙与达尔文主义相互交织的结果。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Edwin Drinker Cope, who's a Quaker from Pennsylvania, who's brought up with a kind of literal belief in Genesis and the flood and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫爱德温·德林克·科普，是宾夕法尼亚州的一个贵格会教徒，从小接受对《创世记》、大洪水以及所有这类事情的字面信仰。

sentences.en: But he's also obsessed by natural history.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也对自然历史着迷。

sentences.en: And as the Western frontier is being pushed ever further towards the Pacific, so he goes in its wake.
sentences.zh: 随着西部前沿不断向太平洋推进，他也随之而去。

sentences.en: So along with all the buffalo hunters and the prospectors and all those kind of people, Cope is riding out into the Wild West looking for dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 因此，伴随着所有的水牛猎人、勘探者和类似的人，科普骑马驰骋在狂野的西部寻找恐龙。

sentences.en: And he's out there in 1877 in the Bighorn Mountains when Custer gets wiped out and it doesn't stop him from, you know, he's dodging the Sioux war bands and so on.
sentences.zh: 1877年，当卡斯特全军覆没时，他正在那里的大角山，但这并没有阻止他，他躲避着苏族的战争帮派等等。

sentences.en: And he ends up having these terrible nightmares in which dinosaurs kind of appear and jostle him and trample him down.
sentences.zh: 他最终开始做这些可怕的噩梦，梦里恐龙出现、推挤他、践踏他。

sentences.en: And I think that that's kind of expressive of this anxiety he has about whether, basically whether evolution, which he's coming to accept,
sentences.zh: 我认为这表达了他的一种焦虑，即他开始接受的进化论，

sentences.en: can be squared with belief in a kind of loving God.
sentences.zh: 是否能与对一个慈爱的上帝的信仰调和。

sentences.en: And it imposes ever greater strains on him.
sentences.zh: 这给他施加了越来越大的压力。

sentences.en: And he ends up, essentially, he leaves the society of friends.
sentences.zh: 他最终本质上脱离了贵格会社团。

sentences.en: He gives up his Quaker faith.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了他的贵格会信仰。

sentences.en: And he actually kind of becomes a racist because the only way that he can justify believing in the benefits of God is if he argues, basically, that every human,
sentences.zh: 他实际上变成了一个种族主义者，因为他能证明上帝美意的唯一方式，就是主张整个人类、

sentences.en: every living organism has a kind of end point that has been defined by God.
sentences.zh: 每一个有生命的生物都有一个由上帝界定的终点。

sentences.en: And so every, all species are kind of inexorably moving towards it.
sentences.zh: 因此所有物种都在不可阻挡地朝着这个终点移动。

sentences.en: And if that's the case, then that must be true of human beings.
sentences.zh: 如果情况确实如此，那么这对人类也必定成立。

sentences.en: And therefore, you know, people like him must be way up, further up the evolutionary train than people who don't know about evolution.
sentences.zh: 因此，像他这样的人必定在进化链条上远远高于那些不了解进化论的人。

sentences.en: So he becomes kind of scientific racist, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上变成了一个科学种族主义者。

sentences.en: He becomes a scientific racist despite himself.
sentences.zh: 他违心地变成了一个科学种族主义者。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't want, you know, he has, he kind of abandons his belief that all, you know, this Quaker conviction that all human beings have a kind of fundamental dignity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他并不想——他抛弃了那种认为所有人、这种贵格会关于所有人都有基本尊严的信念。

sentences.en: He ends up losing it.
sentences.zh: 他最终失去了它。

sentences.en: But Cope is also famous for what is one of the most notorious rivalries in science, which he has with another American scientist, a man called Charles Ophniel Marsh.
sentences.zh: 但科普也因科学史上最声名狼藉的竞争之一而闻名，这是他与另一位美国科学家查尔斯·奥思尼尔·马什之间的竞争。
zh_words: 查尔斯·奥思尼尔·马什之间

sentences.en: And he's also going out, he absolutely, he's untroubled by Darwinism.
sentences.zh: 他也去野外，他完全不受达尔文主义的困扰。

sentences.en: And he discovers what is one of the classic proofs of it, the evolution of the horse.
sentences.zh: 他发现了达尔文主义的最经典证据之一——马的进化。

sentences.en: But, but Marshall also discovers an enormous number of dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 但马什也发现了数量庞大的恐龙。

sentences.en: So between them, they're discovering loads of the classics, kind of, you know, all the long-necked ones, the sauropods.
sentences.zh: 所以在他们两人之间，他们发现了大量经典恐龙，你知道的，所有长脖子的蜥脚类恐龙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Triceratops, all these kind of ones, because it turns out,
sentences.zh: 三角龙，所有这些种类的恐龙，因为事实证明，

sentences.en: and I think that this is a kind of wonderful way in which dinosaurs provide a brilliant metaphor for 19th and 20th century history.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种奇妙的方式，恐龙为19和20世纪的历史提供了一个绝妙的隐喻。

sentences.en: But as industrial supremacy is leeching from Britain to the United States, so also does the leap in paleontology.
sentences.zh: 但随着工业霸权从英国流向美国，古生物学的飞跃也随之发生。

sentences.en: Because it turns out that, you know, that in the West, these lands that are being opened up by the army, there are enormous numbers of dinosaurs, and you can dig them up.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，在西部，军队开辟的这些土地上，有数量惊人的恐龙，你可以把它们挖出来。

sentences.en: Now, why is that?
sentences.zh: 现在，这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Is it something to do with the soil, or what's the story?
sentences.zh: 这和土壤有关，还是背后有什么故事？

sentences.en: It's to do with the geology, it's to do with, it's to do with the fact that, you know, there aren't kind of picturesque villages everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这与地质有关，与到处没有风景如画的村庄这一事实有关。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's right the way, so all along the Rockies, right the way up to Canada, there are just enormous, enormous numbers of dinosaurs waiting to be found.
sentences.zh: 情况一直如此，沿着落基山脉一直到加拿大，都有数量巨大、数不胜数的恐龙等待着被发现。

sentences.en: And Martian Cope, you know, there are so many that basically they, you know, I mean, it's kind of, it's a brilliant metaphor for American capitalism,
sentences.zh: 而马什和科普，你知道的，数量如此之多以至于他们基本上，你知道的，我的意思是，这简直是美国资本主义的一个绝妙隐喻，

sentences.en: because they compete with each other so brutally, you know, they would rather smash bones up than need them to be discovered by the other guy.
sentences.zh: 因为他们彼此竞争得如此残酷，宁愿把骨头砸碎也不愿让对方发现它们。

sentences.en: And they end up kind of, both of them kind of basically bankrupt, a monopolist moves in and buys up all their stuff, and that monopolist is Andrew Carnegie.
sentences.zh: 他们最终两败俱伤，几乎双双破产，一个垄断者介入并买下了他们所有的东西，那个垄断者就是安德鲁·卡内基。

sentences.en: Yeah, you couldn't make that up, could you?
sentences.zh: 对，你简直编不出这样的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's just a perfect metaphor.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是个完美的隐喻。

sentences.en: And Andrew Carnegie is interested, I mean, he's not interested in paleontology for his own sake, he's interested in massive dinosaurs that will make a huge statement.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·卡内基感兴趣的——我的意思是，他对古生物学本身不感兴趣，他对能产生巨大影响的庞大恐龙感兴趣。

sentences.en: He wants a dinosaur that is as big as his own kind of industrial ambitions.
sentences.zh: 他想要一只和他的工业野心一样大的恐龙。

sentences.en: And so he buys one called Diplodocus, that is the, at that point, the longest dinosaur that had ever been discovered.
sentences.zh: 所以他买下了一只名为梁龙的恐龙，那是当时发现的最长的恐龙。

sentences.en: He buys it up, he names it after himself.
sentences.zh: 他买下了它，并用自己的名字给它命名。

sentences.en: Why do you say Diplodocus and not Diplodocus?
sentences.zh: 你为什么说“Diplodocus”而不是“Diplodocus”？

sentences.en: I don't know, I just always know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，我一直这么叫。

sentences.en: Okay, I was just brought up as a Diplodocus man, and I've tried to instill that in youngsters that I meet.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我从小就被当成“Diplodocus”派培养，我也试图向我遇到的年轻人灌输这一点。

sentences.en: But, you know, I don't know what the correct pronunciation is.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我不知道正确的发音是什么。

sentences.en: Okay, this is a sort of Cope Marsh type feud.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一场类似科普与马什式的宿怨。

sentences.en: So, and then what Carnegie does is he makes casts of it, and he sends it first of all to London, so that's the one that was in the Natural History Museum for a long time.
sentences.zh: 然后卡内基的做法是制作它的铸模，首先把它送到伦敦，这就是长期在自然历史博物馆展出的那一具。

sentences.en: Yeah, which we all remember, you know, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，我们都记得，没错。

sentences.en: But he does other casts and he sends it round.
sentences.zh: 但他制作了其他铸模并四处发送。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of wonderful illustration of the way, you know, Carnegie himself is from Scotland originally.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个极好的例证，卡内基本人最初来自苏格兰。

sentences.en: So it's just, the industry is passing from the old world to the new, and the new is now starting to export it back to the old.
sentences.zh: 所以，工业正从旧世界向新世界转移，而新世界现在开始将它出口回旧世界。

sentences.en: It's kind of a perfect illustration of it.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是它的一个完美图解。

sentences.en: It's that at this point, the idea of dinosaurs as slow, lumbering, dumb, hopeless creatures that have gone extinct because they've been wiped out by mammals hasn't kicked in yet.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，将恐龙视为行动迟缓、笨拙、愚蠢、无可救药的生物，因为被哺乳动物消灭而灭绝的观念还没有流行起来。

sentences.en: So it's still fine for Carnegie to associate a dinosaur with his own industrial concerns, as it is with the Sinclair Oil Company, which takes as its logo a sauropod, a dinosaur.
sentences.zh: 因此，卡内基将恐龙与他自己的工业利益联系起来完全没有问题，就像辛克莱石油公司将其标志定为蜥脚类恐龙一样。

sentences.en: And we're about to get to the point of, with T-Rex, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 我们马上就要讲到霸王龙了，对吧？

sentences.en: The discovery of Tyrannosaurus rex, and this extraordinary man, Barnum Brown, who went around in long fur coats and was a great sort of showman.
sentences.zh: 暴龙的发现，以及这个非凡的人，巴纳姆·布朗，他总是穿着长皮毛大衣，是一个非常了不起的表演奇才。

sentences.en: And so what's the story with him?
sentences.zh: 那么关于他的故事是什么？

sentences.en: Is he a real paleontologist?
sentences.zh: 他是一个真正的古生物学家吗？

sentences.en: Or the very word Barnum kind of makes me think he's just running a circus or something.
sentences.zh: 还是“巴纳姆”这个名字本身就让我觉得他只是在经营马戏团之类的地方。

sentences.en: Well, he's from the Bachelor History Museum in New York.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他来自纽约的自然历史博物馆。

sentences.en: Mr. Bones.
sentences.zh: 骨头先生。

sentences.en: Is that how they call him Mr. Bones?
sentences.zh: 他们是这么叫他的吗，骨头先生？

sentences.en: Well, he's a showman in the way that, you know, Buffalo Bill is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他就像水牛比尔那样是一个表演奇才。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, this is still kind of the age where the mythology of the West is still incredibly current and he makes play with it, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这仍然是一个西部神话极其盛行的时代，他善于利用这一点，你知道的，

sentences.en: and he is the Eastern gentleman going out WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他就是前往西部的东部绅士。

sentences.en: So that's why he's wearing fur coat.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他穿着皮大衣。

sentences.en: And also he's incredibly predatory because he discovers actually that the best fossil deposits are up in Canada.
sentences.zh: 而且他极其具有掠夺性，因为他实际上发现最好的化石矿床在加拿大。

sentences.en: And that in no way stops him from taking all the bones and sending them to New York.
sentences.zh: 但这丝毫不妨碍他把所有的骨头都拿走并运到纽约。

sentences.en: And you're starting to get the sense that, you know, America's global ambitions are manifesting themselves through the appetite of American paleontologists for fossils.
sentences.zh: 你开始感觉到，美国的全球野心正在通过美国古生物学家对化石的渴望展现出来。

sentences.en: So you've got Barnum Brown kind of digging up T-Rexes, such-like creatures, all the way up the West, deep into Canada.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到巴纳姆·布朗一路向西、深入加拿大，去挖掘霸王龙之类的生物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then in the 20s, you have this guy, Roy Chapman Andrews, who is the guy who discovers the protoceratops eggs.
sentences.zh: 然后在20年代，你有了这个人，罗伊·查普曼·安德鲁斯，也就是发现原角龙蛋的人。

sentences.en: So he goes on a series of kind of amazing expeditions to the flaming cliffs in the Gobi Desert.
sentences.zh: 因此他去戈壁滩的火焰崖进行了一系列惊人的探险。

sentences.en: And he, it is said, I don't know how accurately, is one of the models for Indiana Jones.
sentences.zh: 据说——我不知道准确性如何——他是印第安纳·琼斯的原型之一。

sentences.en: He's, you know, he's got a whip and...
sentences.zh: 他，你知道的，他拿着鞭子……

sentences.en: He's fighting to snakes, fights Nazis.
sentences.zh: 他与蛇搏斗，与纳粹战斗。

sentences.en: All that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有类似的事情。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of, you know, it's still, it's something that men of action want to be associated with.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个，你知道的，这仍然是动作英雄们想要与之产生关联的事物。

sentences.en: But again, to pursue this idea that dinosaurs provide a metaphor for the process of capitalism and industrialization, in the Great Crash, so in the Depression,
sentences.zh: 但同样，为了延续“恐龙为资本主义和工业化进程提供隐喻”这一观点，在大崩溃期间，也就是大萧条时期，

sentences.en: you increasingly start to get the sense that actually dinosaurs are a bit of a dead end, that they are properly for children,
sentences.zh: 你越来越开始感觉到，实际上恐龙有点像是死胡同，它们真正属于小孩子，

sentences.en: and that dinosaurs themselves are kind of evolutionary dead ends that don't really matter.
sentences.zh: 而且恐龙本身就是某种无关紧要的进化死胡同。

sentences.en: They're ponderous and slow and lumbering.
sentences.zh: 它们笨重、缓慢又迟钝。

sentences.en: And I think that that's an image of them.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这就是对它们的印象。

sentences.en: It's still kind of just about current to this day.
sentences.zh: 而且这种印象至今依然差不多存在。

sentences.en: To pick up one of our previous podcasts, in GoldenEye, M calls James Bond a racist, misogynist dinosaur.
sentences.zh: 接着我们之前的一期播客，在《黄金眼》里，M把詹姆斯·邦德称为一个有种族歧视和厌女情结的老古董。

sentences.en: Of course, dinosaurs were neither racist nor misogynist, were they?
sentences.zh: 当然，恐龙既没有种族歧视，也没有厌女情结，对吧？

sentences.en: But, well, to go from Bond to something he knew a lot about, the Cold War, there comes to be this interesting kind of thing with communist and capitalist dinosaurs, doesn't there?
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，从邦德转向他非常了解的一个领域——冷战，这里就产生了一种关于共产主义和资本主义恐龙的有趣现象，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, in the Soviet Union, dinosaurs are imagined differently from how they are in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，在苏联，人们对恐龙的想象与西方截然不同。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, if you think the classic image of a Mesozoic scene, which has been replayed in countless numbers of films, the classic image, perhaps, is a Tyrannosaur against a Triceratops.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想到中生代场景的经典形象，这个场景在无数电影中被重现过，那经典的形象，也许就是暴龙对阵三角龙。

sentences.en: You always get them.
sentences.zh: 你总能看到这样的画面。

sentences.en: You know, the Triceratops with the three horns, the Tyrannosaur with the giant teeth, and they fight each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，长着三只角的三角龙，长着巨大牙齿的暴龙，它们互相搏斗。

sentences.en: And in the kind of the classic American illustrations, you have a T-Rex, you have a Triceratops, and it's like a kind of shootout in some Wild West town outside the saloon.
sentences.zh: 在那种经典的美国插画里，你会看到一只霸王龙，一只三角龙，就像是某个美国西部小镇酒吧外的一场枪战。

sentences.en: It's the sheriff against the bad guy.
sentences.zh: 这就是治安官对决恶人。

sentences.en: Who's the sheriff?
sentences.zh: 谁是治安官？

sentences.en: The Triceratops?
sentences.zh: 三角龙吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I guess the Triceratops is the sheriff.
sentences.zh: 是的，我猜三角龙就是治安官。

sentences.en: He's seeing off the battle rustler.
sentences.zh: 它正在赶走牛群强盗。

sentences.en: In the Soviet Union, there was a famous artist called Konstantinovich Slayerov, and he, during Operation Barbarossa, as the Nazis were laying siege to Leningrad,
sentences.zh: 在苏联，有一位著名的艺术家叫康斯坦丁诺维奇·斯莱耶罗夫，在巴巴罗萨行动期间，当纳粹对列宁格勒进行围困时，

sentences.en: he was in Leningrad, I think, or maybe he was in Moscow, I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 他当时在列宁格勒，我想是的，或者可能在莫斯科，我记不清了。

sentences.en: Anyway, he was in one of them, and he did a spectacular illustration of a T-Rex Triceratops face-off.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，他当时在其中一个城市里，画了一幅壮观的霸王龙与三角龙对峙的插图。

sentences.en: What he did was to have a whole number of Triceratopses, and they've kind of formed a phalanx so that their horns bristle like spears.
sentences.zh: 他是这样画的：有一大群三角龙，它们排成了一个方阵，它们的角像长矛一样根根直立。

sentences.en: And there are three kind of predatory Tyrannosaurs circling it, but they can't break in.
sentences.zh: 周围有三只掠食性的霸王龙在盘旋，但它们无法突破防线。

sentences.en: So, unlike in the American, where you have Triceratops as a kind of lone gun, in the Soviet version, they're a collective.
sentences.zh: 所以，与美国版本中把三角龙描绘成独行枪手不同，在苏联版本里，它们是一个集体。

sentences.en: Because the Soviet army gets to see off Hitler, so the Triceratops get to see off Tyrannosaurs.
sentences.zh: 因为苏联军队击退了希特勒，所以三角龙也击退了霸王龙。

sentences.en: And I think it's kind of really, it does show how readily, you know, the prehistoric world lends itself to kind of all kinds of metaphors like that.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这真的很能说明问题，史前世界确实很容易让人联想到各种各样的这类隐喻。

sentences.en: But the field of understanding dinosaurs, I mean, the history of it is, as you've shown, fascinating, but it didn't stop being fascinating, did it?
sentences.zh: 但是，理解恐龙的领域，我的意思是，正如你所展示的，它的历史非常迷人，而且它并没有停止变得迷人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because am I right in thinking in the 60s and 70s, or maybe I'm a bit early, maybe 70s and 80s, there were huge kind of convulsions in the study of dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 因为我没记错的话，在20世纪60和70年代，或者可能我记早了一点，也许是70和80年代，恐龙研究领域发生了巨大的动荡。

sentences.en: So, people had thought they were cold-blooded, and then they thought they were warm-blooded.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们原以为它们是冷血动物，后来又认为它们是温血动物。

sentences.en: They had thought they're reptiles, and then they basically think they're birds.
sentences.zh: 人们曾以为它们是爬行动物，然后基本上认为它们是鸟类。

sentences.en: You must know tons about this, because you're very into this dinosaurs and birds business, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 你对这方面一定很了解，因为你对恐龙和鸟类的事很感兴趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, you quoted Bob Bakker at the beginning of this episode, and he wrote a famous book called The Dinosaur Heresies,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你在本集开头引用了鲍勃·巴克的话，他写过一本著名的书叫《恐龙异说》，

sentences.en: in which absolutely, you say, he argued that dinosaurs were warm-blooded, that they were mobile, that they were incredibly successful.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他在书中绝对地主张恐龙是温血动物，它们行动敏捷，而且极其成功。

sentences.en: At the back of this was a discovery made in the 60s of a dinosaur called Deinonychus.
sentences.zh: 这背后的契机是60年代发现了一种名为恐爪龙的恐龙。

sentences.en: Actually, Deinonychus had been discovered earlier, but it's a guy called John Ostrom argues that Deinonychus means terrible claw.
sentences.zh: 其实恐爪龙更早就被发现了，但有个叫约翰·奥斯特伦姆的人提出，恐爪龙的意思是可怕的爪子。

sentences.en: And these were very mobile, they seemed to attack in packs, they could run, they could jump, so they were the opposite of Ponderous.
sentences.zh: 这些动物非常敏捷，似乎是成群结队地攻击，它们会跑会跳，所以它们完全是笨重的反义词。

sentences.en: And he extrapolated from this an argument that dinosaurs were just kind of basically terrifying.
sentences.zh: 他由此推断出这样一个观点：恐龙基本上就是……让人感到恐惧的。

sentences.en: And it's Deinonychus that is Velociraptor in Jurassic Park, because Velociraptor sounds more frightening.
sentences.zh: 而《侏罗纪公园》里的迅猛龙其实就是恐爪龙，因为迅猛龙听起来更吓人。

sentences.en: So, and also, obviously, Deinonychus bears a very strong resemblance to birds.
sentences.zh: 所以，而且很明显，恐爪龙与鸟类有着极高的相似性。

sentences.en: And this was something that wasn't original to Ostrom.
sentences.zh: 这不是奥斯特伦姆原创的想法。

sentences.en: Actually, Thomas Huxley, who was...
sentences.zh: 实际上，托马斯·赫胥黎，也就是……

sentences.en: Darwin's bulldog.
sentences.zh: 达尔文的斗犬。

sentences.en: Yes, a good titanic figure of late Victorian science.
sentences.zh: 对，维多利亚时代晚期科学界的泰斗级人物。

sentences.en: He had argued that the birds were basically dinosaurs, but that was an argument that got Park, but it gets revived in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 他曾主张鸟类基本上就是恐龙，但这个观点后来被搁置了，不过在60年代又重新复苏了。

sentences.en: And essentially now people would say, so that backer passage, you know, he says dinosaurs are extinct.
sentences.zh: 基本上现在人们会说，你看巴克的那段话，他说恐龙已经灭绝了。

sentences.en: I think most people now, most scientists, and I speak completely as a non-scientist, would say that dinosaurs aren't extinct, because birds are dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 我想现在大多数人，大多数科学家——我完全是以一个非科学家的身份发言——会说恐龙并没有灭绝，因为鸟类就是恐龙。

sentences.en: So they're still around.
sentences.zh: 所以它们依然存在。

sentences.en: So all the old stuff about the death of the dinosaurs is overheated.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有关于恐龙灭绝的陈旧说法都是言过其实的。

sentences.en: And so that is the other thing that happened, was that the great mystery for a century and more was what happened to the dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是另一件发生的事：一个多世纪以来，最大的谜团一直是恐龙身上到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Where did they go?
sentences.zh: 它们去哪儿了？

sentences.en: Why did they become extinct?
sentences.zh: 它们为什么会灭绝？

sentences.en: And so you had all, you know, the Gary Larson, the famous Gary Larson cartoon, terrible news, guys.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到所有这些，你知道的，加里·拉森那幅著名的加里·拉森漫画：伙计们，有个糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: We're complete, you know, we've got brains the size of a walnut and there are loads of mammals taking over.
sentences.zh: 我们彻底完了，你知道的，我们只有核桃般大小的大脑，而有大量哺乳动物正在接管世界。

sentences.en: That was basically why people thought that they were kind of hopeless in the dead end.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是人们认为它们无可救药且走入死胡同的原因。

sentences.en: But it was in the 80s, so in 81, a brother and father team of geologists, Alvarez, Père et Fies,
sentences.zh: 但那是在80年代，所以在1981年，阿尔瓦雷斯父子这对地质学家组合，

sentences.en: identified this kind of strain in the sediment at the end of the Cretaceous period when the dinosaurs go extinct, of iridium,
sentences.zh: 在白垩纪末期恐龙灭绝时的沉积物中，发现了这种铱元素的痕迹，

sentences.en: which seemed to imply that there'd been a kind of an asteroid hit.
sentences.zh: 这似乎暗示曾有过一次小行星撞击。

sentences.en: And they argued that this perhaps was what had killed the dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这或许就是杀死恐龙的原因。

sentences.en: And this was a theory that got kind of stress tested and stress tested and stress tested.
sentences.zh: 这个理论经受了一次又一次、一次又一次的压力测试。

sentences.en: And ultimately, I mean, pretty quickly came to be almost universally accepted.
sentences.zh: 最终，我的意思是，很快它几乎就被全世界所接受了。

sentences.en: And the impact point got discovered.
sentences.zh: 而且撞击点也被发现了。

sentences.en: It's in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 它在墨西哥。

sentences.en: And essentially, the dinosaurs went extinct due to bad luck.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，恐龙的灭绝纯粹是由于运气不好。

sentences.en: But they didn't go extinct if they're still around.
sentences.zh: 但如果它们还活着，那就不能算灭绝。

sentences.en: Okay, so the non-avian dinosaurs went extinct due to bad luck.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么非鸟类恐龙的灭绝是由于运气不好。

sentences.en: So you have this combination of the realisation that dinosaurs have been mobile, lots of them perhaps have been warm-blooded, that they were basically birds,
sentences.zh: 所以你有了这样一种认知结合：认识到恐龙曾行动敏捷，其中许多可能还是温血动物，它们基本上就是鸟类，

sentences.en: combined with the sense that the fact they'd gone extinct wasn't really their fault, which was all of which fused just in time for Spielberg's film Jurassic Park.

sentences.en: And the degree to which that is just a metaphor, whether there's something deeper.

sentences.en: Sorry?
sentences.zh: 不好意思？

sentences.zh: 所以，那仍然，那仍然在某种程度上存在。
